chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
Any Muslim who releases another Muslim from a sale due to his regret, Allah will release him from his stumble on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.أَقَالَ: released or canceled; to revoke the sale and let the other party withdraw
key_terms.أَيُّمَا: whoever; a general conditional expression indicating any person fitting the description
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah; the One who grants recompense and pardon
key_terms.الْبَيْعِ: the sale; the commercial transaction in question
key_terms.عَثْرَتَهُ: his slip or stumble; a figurative expression for error or downfall
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim; here, both the one granting relief and the one receiving it
key_terms.نَدَامَةً: regret; remorse felt over the transaction
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection; the day of final reckoning and recompense

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for canceling a sale when another Muslim regrets it?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the virtue of showing ease and consideration in financial dealings, especially when a buyer or seller regrets a transaction. It links merciful conduct in trade with Allah’s mercy in the hereafter, promising divine pardon on the Day of Resurrection.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3738 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Any Muslim who cancels a sale for another Muslim who regrets it, Allah (swt) will cancel his slip on the Day of Judgment."
